title: Milvus standalone Docker container exits with code 134 during inserts
body: I am running Milvus v2.5.8 standalone in Docker on a machine with 8 CPU cores and 16 GB of memory. The container exits after about one minute with status 134. It worked initially and single-vector inserts succeeded, but during an automated task inserting about 130,000 records one by one, it failed after more than 8,000 inserts. There are many logs; the partial output includes a Go goroutine in IO wait.

symptoms_visible: My Milvus v2.5.8 standalone container exits with status 134 shortly after startup.
It initially accepted individual vector inserts, but my automated one-row-at-a-time workload stopped after more than 8,000 rows.
N0.label: N0 Docker exit 134 reported

symptoms_visible: After I restart the container, it still exits in the same way.
Single inserts worked before, but the larger insertion run causes the server to become unavailable.
N1.label: N1 full logs and repeat behavior collected

symptoms_visible: The existing container still exits with status 134, so I cannot connect through Attu to inspect the collection.
N2.label: N2 schema and storage details collected

symptoms_visible: After deleting the volumes and rebuilding the collection, it crashed again at about 6,059 inserted rows.
Once it crashed, my insert process received connection-refused errors from port 19530.
N2_x.label: N2_x fresh-volume rebuild aftermath

symptoms_visible: With a newly created Attu collection where I selected only Nullable and did not enable auto index or a tokenizer, Milvus still exited with status 134 at around 6,000 to 7,000 rows.
N3.label: N3 minimal Attu configuration also reproduced

symptoms_visible: After switching to Milvus v2.5.9 and retrying the workload, I have not seen the status-134 crash recur.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on fixed patch release

question_patterns: Can you export the complete Docker Compose logs, especially the last few minutes before the exit?
Please upload the full Milvus log from a run that ends with status 134.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I uploaded milvus-log.txt. It is quite large.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The container log says it was killed by the kernel OOM killer and contains no Milvus exception.
I uploaded the same complete log from another run, with slightly different goroutine numbers.

question_patterns: Does it start normally after a restart, or does it exit again?
Can you restart the stack once and tell me whether the failure repeats?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I restarted it and the result is still the same.

edges.comment: Reporter c3, responding to maintainer c1-c2: the original reporter uploaded the complete log and stated that a restart produced the same result. The std::logic_error interpretation was made later by the maintainer and is not placed in the reporter's answer.

question_patterns: How did you create the collection and its indexes?
Can you share the collection-creation and index-creation code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created the collection and schema by clicking through the Attu graphical tool, so I do not have collection-creation code to share.

question_patterns: What fields and data types are in the collection schema?
Please list the vector and scalar fields in the Attu collection.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The schema has an int64 ID, a float vector generated with BGE, and several varchar fields for Chinese address components: tw, ps, nc, standard_addr and an allc field containing the components joined together.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The collection contains only an int64 primary key and one float-vector field; it has no varchar or other scalar fields.

question_patterns: Does your collection have the standard_addr field mentioned in the log?
Can you confirm the name of the long address field?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I have a standard_addr field.

question_patterns: Did you create a scalar index or enable any index option for the varchar fields?
Do you remember whether Attu created an automatic scalar index?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot see the previous settings now. I do not remember whether it was an auto index; I may have checked the scalar-index option because I am new to this.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I explicitly created only a BITMAP index on the varchar field and never used automatic, hybrid, or inverted indexing.
I still cannot remember the exact Attu checkbox, but I may have accepted its default scalar-index setting.

question_patterns: Can you share the code used to insert the rows?
How are you constructing each row and its vector?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My loop joins the Chinese address fields, generates a BGE document embedding, converts the dense vector to numpy float16, and calls insert_embeddings with one row at a time.

question_patterns: Can you look in the mounted persistent volume and locate the collection and segment files?
Please show what files are present under the Docker volume.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found the files in the mounted volume. I attached a screenshot; which file do you need?

edges.comment: Reporter c7-c20, answering maintainers c4, c6, c8, c13, c15 and c17: the original reporter described the Attu-created schema, uncertainty about scalar indexing, insertion loop, and mounted files. No setup or evidence from the later second affected user is merged here.

solution.intent: Delete the persisted volumes, rebuild the collection from scratch with the demonstrated schema, and repeat the inserts in case the original deployment state is corrupt.
solution.concrete_example: Stop the stack, remove the volumes directory, create the collection again, and rerun the same insertion workload to see whether the crash reproduces.

edges.comment: Maintainer zhuwenxing c21 suggested deleting the volumes and repeating the operation. The original reporter c22-c23 rebuilt and reproduced the failure after 6,059 rows, so resetting persisted data was falsified as a durable fix.

question_patterns: Can you recreate the Attu collection without selecting optional matching, analyzer, or index settings and show the selected options?
Please try a minimal schema configuration and report exactly which Attu checkboxes are enabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created another collection in Attu and selected only Nullable. I did not select the other options.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With only Nullable enabled, the same workload completed all rows and the container stayed up; it crashes only when the analyzer and automatic index options are enabled.
I enabled only Nullable in a second minimal collection and got the same result at about 7,200 rows.

question_patterns: What happens when you rerun the inserts with no automatic index and no tokenizer enabled?
Does the minimal Attu configuration still exit around the same row count?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Even when I enable neither auto index nor the tokenizer, it still exits with error 134 at around 6,000 to 7,000 rows.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Without auto index and the tokenizer it completed the full data set; enabling either option makes it crash.

question_patterns: What encoding is the input data using, and can you provide a nonsensitive example value?
Are all of the varchar values valid UTF-8?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The data is UTF-8 Chinese address data, for example a value like '上海市上海市浦东新区川沙镇XX路◇1xx弄12号1003***'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing rows contain invalid byte sequences and are not valid UTF-8.

edges.comment: Original reporter c22-c29, following maintainers c24, c27 and c28: the reporter compared Attu configurations, reported the raw row-count outcome, and supplied a sanitized UTF-8 address example. The first-flush and index-path interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Treat the abort as a Milvus server bug in the VARCHAR/scalar indexing work reached around flush, update the standalone image to the maintainer-identified fixed patch release, and have the reporter rerun the affected workload before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the v2.5.8 image with Milvus v2.5.9, redeploy the standalone stack, and rerun the same Chinese-address insertion workload. Confirm that it passes the previous 6,000-8,000-row failure point without an exit-134 abort.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied logs, schema details, repeated row-count failures, and UTF-8 samples. Maintainers interpreted the log as std::logic_error in the scalar/VARCHAR index path and associated the 6,000-8,000-row timing with the first flush. The exact internal diagnosis and identification of the fixed patch release are engineer-side conclusions, not facts the reporter independently derived.

edges.comment: Maintainers c27-c38 connected the timing to flush and the logs to the VARCHAR/inverted or hybrid scalar-index path, then corrected the recommended fixed release from a typo of v2.4.9 to v2.5.9. The original reporter c39 tested v2.5.9 and reported no current recurrence. KendrickChou's separate setup and tests are corroborating context only and are not substituted for the original reporter's verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical cause at the level established by the thread: a Milvus server bug in the VARCHAR/scalar indexing path, reached around flush and observed as std::logic_error followed by exit status 134.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the uploaded server log, the VARCHAR-heavy Attu schema, and repeated crashes around 6,000-8,000 inserts, including reproduction after rebuilding from fresh volumes.
Must recommend updating the affected deployment to the maintainer-identified fixed patch release rather than treating additional memory or a volume reset as the established resolution.
Must not present deleting volumes and recreating the same collection as the durable fix; that move was tried and the crash recurred after 6,059 rows.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the previously failing insertion workload on a build containing the server-side fix and only treat the issue as resolved after the reporter reports no recurrence.

persona_hint.experience_level: Beginner Milvus and Docker user who can operate Attu, inspect mounted volumes, edit an image tag, run Python insertion code, and follow reproduction instructions, but is unfamiliar with scalar-index terminology and cannot safely share sensitive address data.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and persistent, mixing Chinese and English; provides code, row counts, screenshots, and sanitized examples, while openly stating uncertainty about earlier Attu settings.
